title: UFO Part 03
what_is_it: Collection of FBI investigative reports, teletypes, and sworn statements from July–October 1947 concerning flying disc sightings, the Maury Island incident, a coded newspaper message, and an internal FBI memo questioning the Bureau's role in flying disc investigations.
interpretation_warnings: Heavy redaction throughout: nearly all witness names, interviewer names, and many organizational affiliations are redacted, making independent verification of specific individuals impossible.
OCR quality is very poor due to aged, degraded scan quality — many passages are partially illegible, and some details may be misread or missing.
The Maury Island incident described in the teletypes was later widely regarded as a hoax; the documents themselves note participants planned to say 'the entire story was a hoax.'
The newspaper pilot's sighting is single-observer with no photographic evidence (film showed nothing), though partial ground corroboration is claimed.
The Hamilton Field sighting lasted only approximately four seconds by the witness's own estimate.
The coded 'Radio Ham' message was assessed by both the newspaper editor and FBI as likely from a 'screwball' — it has no investigative value regarding actual flying discs.
The FBI internal memo reveals institutional reluctance and inter-agency friction rather than objective assessment of the phenomena.

dated_events: 26 June 1947 — original flying disc sighting report over Cascade Mountains
6 July 1947 — newspaper pilot receives aerial search assignment
7 July 1947 — first search flight covering Hanford plant, Mt. Rainier, Mt. Adams area (negative)
8 July 1947 — second search flight to northern Idaho, Montana, Spokane, Pendleton (negative); Hamilton Field sighting of three objects
9 July 1947 — third search flight, pilot sights black round object near Boise/Meridian
10 July 1947 — check made in Palm Springs to locate individual
12 July 1947 — interviews of newspaper pilot and United Airlines pilot in Boise; sworn statement signed
15 July 1947 — interview of military officer at Hamilton Field
21 July 1947 — Bureau letter regarding coded message; Colonel requests FBI flying disc investigation
31 July 1947 — meeting at Winthrop Hotel, Tacoma regarding disc fragments
1 August 1947 — Captain Davidson and Lieutenant Brown depart Tacoma in B-25, killed in crash at Kelso
4 September 1947 — New York FBI office letter re coded message
17 September 1947 — FBI internal memo on coded message investigation
8 October 1947 — J. Edgar Hoover declines information request from Heber, California
objects_described: Black, round object performing erratic jerky flight and partial barrel roll at approximately 14,000 feet near Boise
Three objects northeast over Hamilton Field — two round, light gray, one rotating/rolling behind, altitude 8-10,000 feet
Flying discs reported by United Airlines pilots on July 4 flight from Boise
AT-6 aircraft (Idaho National Guard, used for search flights)
B-25 bomber (crashed at Kelso carrying intelligence officers)
Rock formations from Maury Island alleged to be disc fragments
